rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is whether a core multimodal multiprofile pipeline is competitive. config_013 tests a central, moderately strong hypothesis: scGPT RNA representations plus ResNet-50 image features, multiprofile avgpool aggregation, and simple concat fusion. This avoids the highest-cost choices (ViT-L and transformer aggregation) while still probing the likely best modality combination and a strong RNA encoder. It gives an anchor for deciding whether to escalate to stronger image/aggregation/fusion settings or pivot to cheaper encoders. Expected relative cost: medium-low among multimodal multiprofile options, more expensive than unimodal, singleprofile, or PCA-based configs, but cheaper than ViT-L or transformer-aggregation configs.

The only completed experiment (config_013) provides a weak baseline at 51.2% validation accuracy using scGPT, ResNet50, avgpool, and concat fusion. The key uncertainty is whether concat fusion is optimal or whether weighted fusion can better balance the modalities while keeping the rest of the architecture fixed. config_010 changes only fusion from concat to weighted, so it isolates that design choice and directly extends the current best setting. Its expected cost is similar to config_013, about 4.3 GPU hours, and much lower than ViT-L or transformer-aggregation options, making it a cheap, high-information next step before investing in more expensive upgrades.

The two completed experiments show that multimodal multiprofile models with scGPT, ResNet50, and avgpool are promising, with weighted fusion slightly better than concat on both accuracy and F1. The key uncertainty is whether the current ResNet50 image encoder is limiting performance. Testing config_016 keeps the current best components (scGPT, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) while upgrading only the image encoder to ViT-L, isolating that design choice. This is a strong exploitation step while still reducing uncertainty about a major modality representation, and it avoids confounding multiple changes. Expected relative cost is moderately higher than the completed ~4.4 GPU-hour runs due to the larger ViT-L, but lower than transformer-aggregation or combined transformer/ViT-L configurations.

The best result so far is config_016 (scGPT + ViT-L + avgpool + weighted, accuracy 0.542), indicating that the stronger image encoder and weighted fusion are promising. The key remaining uncertainty for this top direction is aggregation: avgpool has been tested, but transformer aggregation may better model multiprofile interactions. Testing config_019 keeps the strongest known components while directly probing whether transformer aggregation improves accuracy. Expected cost is moderate-to-high, likely somewhat above config_016's 2.94 GPU hours due to transformer aggregation, but still reasonable with 6 experiments remaining.

The strongest evidence so far is config_016, which uses scgpt + ViT-L + avgpool + weighted and has the best validation accuracy (0.542) at low cost. Weighted fusion was better than concat for ResNet50 under the same RNA/aggregation settings, but concat has not been tested with the stronger ViT-L encoder. config_017 isolates this fusion choice under the current best image/aggregation setup, clarifying whether weighted fusion is truly required or whether concat can match/improve it. This is a cheap exploitation of the most promising local neighborhood, with expected cost similar to config_016, about 3 GPU hours and lower than the ResNet50 runs.

The strongest evidence so far is config_016: multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, ViT-L, avgpool, weighted fusion, with the best validation accuracy (0.542) at moderate cost (2.94 GPU hours). Transformer aggregation and concat fusion have underperformed in comparable settings, so the most promising remaining uncertainty is whether scgpt is the best RNA encoder when paired with the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. config_045 tests this directly by keeping ViT-L, avgpool, and weighted fusion while replacing scgpt with scvi_n200. It is expected to have comparable or slightly lower cost than config_016 because the ViT-L and aggregation pipeline likely dominate training time, making it an efficient exploitation step that can either improve the best accuracy or confirm scgpt as the preferred RNA encoder.

The strongest evidence is config_045 (scvi_n200 + ViT-L + avgpool + weighted), which is far ahead of all scgpt-based runs with 0.706 validation accuracy and 0.667 F1. Weighted fusion has also consistently outperformed concat in completed pairs, so the main remaining uncertainty in this promising family is whether transformer aggregation over multiple profiles can improve on avgpool for the scvi_n200 + ViT-L combination. This experiment tests that directly while keeping the best-supported RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion strategy. It is the best next use of the budget because it is a close, high-potential extension of the current best configuration and leaves two experiments for fallbacks if it does not improve. Expected relative cost is moderate, roughly comparable to config_045 and perhaps modestly higher due to transformer aggregation, but still affordable within the remaining budget.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is far better than scgpt, and within that family transformer aggregation with weighted fusion is currently best (config_024: 0.725 accuracy, 0.685 F1), while avgpool weighted is close (config_045: 0.706). The main remaining uncertainty in this promising region is whether concat fusion with transformer aggregation can match or exceed weighted fusion. config_018 tests exactly this by keeping the best RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation while changing fusion to concat. It is the best next experiment because it is a direct, low-risk exploitation of the strongest configuration family, may reveal a higher-accuracy or cost-comparable variant, and leaves two experiments to follow up on any improvement. Expected relative cost is comparable to config_024, roughly 3.5-4.0 GPU hours, and likely similar to or slightly cheaper than the weighted-fusion variant.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 + ImageNet ViT-L multimodal models are far better than scgpt-based ones, with the best result at 0.725 using multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. However, all completed experiments are multiprofile, so the effect of profile setting is an important unresolved uncertainty. config_039 tests whether the same strong RNA and image encoders with weighted fusion can match or beat the multiprofile model in a singleprofile setting, clarifying whether multiprofile aggregation is adding useful signal or unnecessary cost/complexity. This is a good use of experiment 9 because it exploits the best-known encoders while probing a major untested design choice before the final experiment. Expected cost is moderate and likely lower than the multiprofile transformer weighted model because it avoids multiprofile aggregation, though it remains nontrivial due to the ViT-L image encoder, roughly comparable to or slightly below config_024's 3.60 GPU hours.

The strongest evidence is that the best configurations are multimodal multiprofile models using scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, with config_024 at 0.7250 accuracy and config_018 at 0.7207. The only untested cell in this top-performing 2x2 aggregation/fusion grid is avgpool + concat, so config_023 directly tests whether this missing combination can match or exceed the current best. It is the best final experiment because it exploits the clearly dominant encoder/profile setting while resolving the last important fusion/aggregation uncertainty. Expected cost is moderate, likely similar to config_045/config_018, around 4-5 GPU hours.
